definitions.gloss: young sansho leaves used as a garnish
definitions.explanation: In cooking, the young leaves of the {山椒|さんしょう} (Japanese pepper) tree, used as a fragrant garnish on soups, grilled fish, and spring dishes. Also refers more generally to the fresh buds or sprouts of any tree.

examples.japanese: {木|き}の{芽|め}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{添|そ}えた→添える：13315_soeru⟧。
examples.english: I added a sprig of kinome.

examples.japanese: ⟦{吸|す}い{物|もの}→吸い物：04990_suimono⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{木|き}の{芽|め}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{一枚|いちまい}→一枚：08889_ichimai⟧のせた。
examples.english: I placed a single kinome leaf on the clear soup.

examples.japanese: {木|き}の{芽|め}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{手|て}のひら→手のひら：05294_tenohira⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{軽|かる}く→軽い：00785_karui⟧たたくと⟦{香|かお}り→香り：00189_kaori⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{立|た}つ→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧。
examples.english: If you clap kinome lightly between your palms, its fragrance comes out.

notes:
{木|き}の{芽|め} (literally "tree bud") most often refers in cooking specifically to young ⟦{山椒|さんしょう}→山椒：12412_sanshou⟧ leaves, prized for their sharp, citrusy fragrance and used as a spring garnish on ⟦{吸|す}い{物|もの}→吸い物：04990_suimono⟧ (clear soup), grilled fish, and bamboo shoot dishes.

USAGE:
A sprig is traditionally clapped once between the palms just before serving to release its aroma. Outside cooking, {木|き}の{芽|め} can refer to the fresh buds of any tree, especially in spring ({木|き}の{芽|め}{時|どき}, the season when trees bud).
